notes: Added: · The app now says which build it is everywhere someone might look. A tauri dev window is labelled VideoMark — dev in the taskbar, carries an amber Development build strip across every page, and its launcher badge reads v0.2.33 · dev; the installed app wears the same badge in a quiet tone. Both badges open Settings → Updates. · Settings → Updates names the running build and puts a Check for updates button beside it, with a Release notes link. A development build may read what is released but will not install it — the updater replaces the installed app, not the window you clicked in — so there the update banner offers Release notes instead of UPDATE. · Canvas selection now has an order. A press takes the object you mean rather than the one painted on top: the image under the pointer first, then a shape, then the text — so an image answers where a shape paints over it, and a shape answers where text covers it. Where that still hides what you want, Alt+click walks behind it: the cue names what the press reached (Shape · 2 of 2 — Alt+click for the next), the object it reaches is pinned to the front and answers the next drag, and a plain press anywhere else puts the order back. The drag and selection checks also re-run against the installed build once it has taken the update, so the app you actually run is the one these fixes were verified on. · Settings → Storage shows what VideoMark is keeping on disk for its own working — temporary files, the pre-rendered effect cache and the daily logs, each with its size and file count — with a total across them and a Clean now button that empties the folder and says what it freed. The effect cache is deliberately left alone: it is what makes the next export skip the work, so only a cache past its own size limit is trimmed. Beside it, Auto-clean leftovers is on by default and explains itself: the app clears its own leftovers on a timer and when it closes, and only files older than a day are ever removed, so an export in progress is never disturbed. Turn it off and a crash’s leftovers wait for you to press Clean now. Clean up during an export says so and touches nothing. · Changed: · The launcher title is now extruded, light-catching type rather than flat text: the same word, with real depth and a slow idle turn, in the app’s own blue. · Fixed: · VideoMark no longer lets its working files pile up until the disk fills. Every export writes intermediates into its temp folder — mixed audio, cycle videos, overlay renders, spilled filter scripts — and takes them away again when the export ends, but every way the app closes hard-exits the process, and a crash or force-quit skips that cleanup entirely, so the files simply stayed. Nothing ever looked in the folder again, and users watched it grow into hundreds of gigabytes. The folder is now swept at startup and on every close, and the release smoke fails on a folder that is not empty, naming the file that leaked. · Clean now also reclaims what the updater leaves behind: each update downloaded its installer into a fresh folder in the system temp directory and kept it there forever, and the daily logs were never trimmed at all. Both are cleared now, logs down to the newest ten.
